clue.text: Superb pilot with Spitfire initially breezes through?

parts.note: an ace is an expert fighter pilot

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: first letter of Spitfire

explanation.surface: A wartime flying ace sails through the sky in his Spitfire.
explanation.definitionFit: To ace an exam or task is to pass it with ease, so it means sails through effortlessly.

clue.text: Area to change enclosing one zoo feature

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area

indicators.note: enclosing means the words before it wrap round the word that follows

parts.note: to vary is to change
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A plan to redevelop part of a zoo, keeping one attraction inside.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside VARY to make VIARY, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviary is a large enclosure for birds, a typical attraction at a zoo.

clue.text: Flailed about having sunk going round lake

indicators.note: going round means the first word encircles the one after it

parts.note: a ship that founders sinks
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone thrashing about after going under near a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounder is to struggle clumsily, thrashing about as if in mud or water.

clue.text: Unlucky incident where Mike in Russia given Putin's head

parts.note: Misha is the Russian pet form of Mikhail, the equivalent of Mike

indicators.note: the head of a word is its leading letter

parts.note: first letter of Putin

explanation.surface: A misfortune befalls a man called Mike in Russia once Putin takes charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike looks like the NATO-alphabet M, but the whole phrase asks what Mike would be called in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is a minor accident, an unlucky event.

clue.text: This — invariably lethal — used for starters in fight?

definitions.text: This — invariably lethal — used for starters in fight?

indicators.note: in places the selected letters inside the word for a fight

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or scrap

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of the words they refer to

parts.note: first letters of This, invariably and lethal

explanation.surface: A deadly weapon that comes out at the start of a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a dagger is lethal and drawn at the start of a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a slim dagger, a weapon that might be pulled at the outset of a knife fight.

clue.text: Stake — not post?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a poker stake put up before the deal
second meaning: the Latin prefix for before, the opposite of post-

explanation.walkthrough: Post looks like a pole beside the stake; it is the Latin for after, whose opposite is ante, before.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is a poker bet, and ante- as in antenatal means before, the opposite of post- as in postnatal.

clue.text: Antiquated shoe's undersurface in to be repaired

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the reworked letters
something repaired has been put back together, here in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the sole is the underside of a shoe

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned shoe whose sole needs mending.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolete means out of date, no longer in use, much like antiquated.

clue.text: Covered dock in Alabama with store and staff

parts.note: AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama
a pen is a sheltered dock, as for submarines
stock is a store of goods

explanation.surface: A sheltered harbour in Alabama with a warehouse and workers.
explanation.walkthrough: Staff looks like the dock's employees; it is a walking stick. 'In Alabama' only places the dock after the state.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpenstock is a long iron-tipped stick used by mountain walkers, a kind of staff.

clue.text: No inclination from military to make allowance for sovereign?

parts.note: No with from military means not military
civil means not military, the opposite of military
a list is the tilt or lean of a ship

explanation.surface: The army offers no leeway in making an allowance for the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Civil List was the annual sum Parliament granted the British monarch to fund the royal household.

clue.text: See 23
United supporters making return journey in chaos?

indicators.note: a return journey goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United
fans are supporters

explanation.surface: Football fans of United heading home from an away game in disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: SNAFU is military slang: Situation Normal, All Fouled Up.
explanation.definitionFit: A snafu is a muddle or confused mess, a state of chaos.

clue.text: Agony and ecstasy surrounding York's flower

indicators.note: surrounding means the preceding pieces wrap round the next one

parts.note: hell is agony
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
Ebor, from Latin Eboracum, is the short name for York

explanation.surface: A York flower that brings both pain and joy.
explanation.walkthrough: Ebor, from the Roman name Eboracum, is the traditional short form for York, seen in the Archbishop of York's signature and the Ebor horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: The hellebore, such as the Christmas rose, is a flowering plant.

clue.text: Kelvin assessed lasciviously becomes agitated

parts.note: K is the symbol for the kelvin
to eye up is to look at someone with desire

explanation.surface: A man called Kelvin gets flustered after being ogled.
explanation.definitionFit: Keyed up means tense and nervous, in a state of agitation.

clue.text: Legendary ruler's blood on courtyard by ancient city

parts.note: one's blood is one's family, kin
a garth is an enclosed yard or cloister garden
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: A mythical king's blood is spilled on a courtyard near an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur is the legendary British monarch of Camelot and the Round Table.

clue.text: A Durbeyfield round the old place not fully dressed?

indicators.note: round means the name wraps about the words that follow

parts.note: Tess is one of the Durbeyfields, Hardy's heroine in Tess of the d'Urbervilles
O is the abbreviation for old
PL is the abbreviation for place

explanation.surface: Hardy's heroine wanders about the old family home only half clothed.
explanation.definitionFit: Topless means bare above the waist, so not wearing all one's clothes.

clue.text: Prisoners into this, a good pandowdy prepared on the outside?

indicators.note: on the outside means the reworked letters sit around the short pieces
a dish prepared is made up, so the dessert's letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Instructions for an apple pandowdy, a baked pudding, as if packing prisoners into it.
explanation.walkthrough: A pandowdy is an American baked apple pudding. The first 'a' is the article, the second goes into the anagram's middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy wagon is a police van used to carry arrested people.

clue.text: Where Neagh is, lough: duck found therein?

parts.note: Lough Neagh is in Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI
L is the abbreviation for lake or lough

explanation.surface: A duck swimming on Lough Neagh.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck looks like the bird on the lough; in cricket a duck is a score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a duck is a score of nothing, and nil also means nothing.

clue.text: Midlands city having name for church in Dublin location?

indicators.note: having one thing for another means a swap of one abbreviation for another in the city

parts.note: Leicester is a city in the English Midlands
N is the abbreviation for name
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A city in the English Midlands whose name crops up in Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: Leinster is the Irish province that contains Dublin, so Dublin is located there.

clue.text: Is it pulled to preserve neck of jumper?

definitions.text: Is it pulled to preserve neck of jumper?

parts.words: Is it pulled to preserve neck of jumper?
parts.note: surface reading: a knitted jumper whose neckline is held by a drawstring
setter's reading: the jumper is a parachutist, and pulling the cord saves his neck

explanation.walkthrough: Jumper suggests a sweater; here it is a parachutist, and preserving one's neck is staying alive.
explanation.definitionFit: The cord a parachutist pulls to open the canopy, saving their life on the way down.

clue.text: Two notes put in played softly before first performance

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the pieces that follow

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for soft
re and mi are notes of the sol-fa scale
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A quiet passage introduced into the score just ahead of opening night.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiere is the first public performance of a play, film or work of music.

clue.text: Swollen head? Say nothing!

parts.note: e.g. means for example, say
O is a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Telling a big-headed person to keep quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A swollen head is conceit, an inflated ego.

clue.text: Song complete about Minoan daughter

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera

indicators.note: about means turned round to run the other way

parts.note: to end is to complete

explanation.surface: An opera singer finishes an aria about a princess of Crete.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariadne was the daughter of King Minos of Crete, who helped Theseus out of the labyrinth.

clue.text: Sailor on island shortly having to take the plane?

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short by its last letter
in an across clue one thing on another sits after it, so the sailor goes second

parts.note: Skye is a Scottish island
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor stranded on a small island must catch a flight home.
explanation.definitionFit: To skyjack is to hijack an aircraft, taking the plane by force.

clue.text: Skin irritation appearing after tin found in grass

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
an itch is a skin irritation

explanation.surface: A rash comes up after a tin is found lying in the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass is not the lawn but British slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass and to snitch are both slang for informing to the police.

clue.text: Explosive inventor's rewritten fable with Elrond

indicators.note: rewritten means the words are set down again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; Elrond is Tolkien's elf lord

explanation.surface: A Tolkien fable featuring Elrond is reworked into a story about an inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel invented dynamite, so he is the inventor of an explosive.

clue.text: Conductor contains transformed current

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An electrical conductor that carries a changed current.
explanation.walkthrough: Conductor and current suggest electricity; the conductor is a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Record to break when finding mountains

indicators.note: to break into something is to get inside it

parts.note: as can mean when
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Setting out to break a record and finding mountains in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are the great mountain range of central Europe.

clue.text: Join force in a predicament

indicators.note: in places one item inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: a fix is a predicament
F is the symbol for force

explanation.surface: A call to sign up for the forces when things are tight.
explanation.definitionFit: To affix is to attach or fasten one thing to another, to join it on.

clue.text: Whiskey chaser? It's a revealing image

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in the NATO alphabet the code word for X follows Whiskey, for W
second meaning: a radiograph that shows bones inside the body

explanation.walkthrough: A chaser looks like a beer drunk after whisky; here it is the word that comes after Whiskey in the radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio code for X comes straight after Whiskey, and the same word names a photograph taken through the body.

clue.text: Exhaust American power restraining Brussels?

indicators.note: restraining means holding something in, so it sits inside

parts.note: US is short for American
P is the symbol for power
Brussels is the seat of the European Union

explanation.surface: American power reining in the EU until it is worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: Brussels stands for the European Union, which has its headquarters there.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhaust a supply is to use it up completely.

clue.text: Presentation by The Who perhaps better suited to The Stones?

definitions.text: Presentation by The Who perhaps better suited to The Stones?

parts.note: surface reading: a show by the band, such as Tommy
setter's reading: stones are rocks, so a form named after rock suits them

explanation.walkthrough: Tommy by The Who is the classic example of the genre; the joke is that the Rolling Stones' name is literally rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock opera is a sung musical drama in rock style, like The Who's Tommy.
